title: FlashAttention bridging interpolator for decode latency smoothing
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Since integrating FlashAttention v3 for a subset of decoder workloads we’ve observed intermittent 5–30ms tail-latency spikes on long-context decode paths compared to the stable v2 baseline. Root cause signals point to abrupt kernel handoffs during per-layer launch selection (shape/quant/layout mismatches) and transient allocator pressure that causes microjitter in early decode steps.

Goal: Implement a lightweight ‘bridging interpolator’ that smooths the transition between chosen kernel variants (v2/v3/mixed) at per-layer granularity during the first N decode tokens. The interpolator will perform an amortized warmup where small synthetic microbatches and conservative launch parameters are used for selected layers, then gracefully shift to the faster target kernel once KV and allocator metrics stabilize.

Design overview:
- Interpolator is a runtime shim layered above the kernel selector that can be enabled per-model or per-route.
- For each layer during the first decode tokens (configurable window, default 8 tokens) we will: 1) detect unstable handoff conditions via a confidence score (based on shape changes, quant flags, workspace delta); 2) if below threshold, launch a guarded ‘micro-launch’ using conservative workspace and prefetch flags; 3) measure kernel latency/allocator churn for that layer over the window; 4) if metrics converge, escalate to full-speed kernel.

Key features: micro-launch mode, per-layer confidence scoring, entropy-aware thresholding (avoid oscillation for stochastic decoding), backoff hysteresis, telemetry hooks (per-layer latency, workspace bytes, alloc/release cycles).

Success criteria:
- Reduce 95th and 99th percentile decode latency for affected models by >=15% vs current v3 rollout on canary fleet while preserving median latency improvement from v3.
- No increase in memory OOM incidents in canary (0 events).
- Canary error rates unchanged (<0.01% delta).

Trade-offs and risks:
- Small additional CPU overhead for confidence scoring and micro-launch orchestration.
- Slightly higher early-token latency for some requests (acceptable if tail improved).
- Complexity in rollout; requires good telemetry and canary gating to avoid oscillation.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for interpolator state machine and confidence scorer.
- Offline replay with synthetic burst profiles (short/long prompts, sampling/beam).
- Lab perf runs across GPU types (A100 80GB, H100) and quantized variants (int8/4bit).
- Canary rollout: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback triggers on latency/regression thresholds.

Rollout plan: implement behind runtime flag and model annotation. Initial canary on internal conversational models then expand to public canary routes.

Open questions: optimal default window size, confidence score composition, how to expose tuning knobs in Console.
